(a) the majority of selfdisclosures on Facebook were positive and entertaining, (b) the more intimate communication took mainly place in private conversations, and (c) positive and entertaining selfdisclosures increased the feeling of connectedness, especially when reading status updates of friends.

(a) the majority of status updates on social network sites are entertaining, (b) entertaining and positive self-disclosures are related to the feeling of connection to the interaction partner and (c) this effect is not mediated by the interaction partner’s responsiveness.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the content of status updates affects users’ feelings of connection.
the question of how social network sites (here: Facebook) can contribute to the formation of social relations, especially in the case of people with few social ties.
the function of self-disclosures on social network sites.

social media is not a threat to relationships but rather a tool to strengthen them, and that it is not just the quantity of communication but rather its quality which determines relational outcomes.
